final_answer: In a free market, price is determined by the interaction of supply and demand. When demand increases, prices rise, encouraging suppliers to produce more. When supply increases, prices fall, allowing consumers to buy more. This equilibrium adjusts continuously. If a government imposes a price ceiling—setting a maximum price below the equilibrium—suppliers may reduce production because they can’t cover costs, leading to shortages. Buyers, however, will want to purchase more at the lower price, creating excess demand. This often results in black markets or reduced quality as suppliers find ways to circumvent the restriction.
